ex:topological-mass-su2:
Example Topological mass decomposition for \mathrm{SU}(2). Continuing the descent eigenspaces for SU(2), one verifies the topological mass conjecture for G = \mathrm{SU}(2).

The decomposition. By the topological mass theorem, the mass of a cycle \varrho decomposes according to the eigenspace splitting:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) =  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) + \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho),

where \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}} = \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \rVert gives the descended (persistent) contribution and \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}} = \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho) \rVert gives the transient contribution.

Descended mass. The descended trace \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}} factors through the projection \hat{\tau} onto \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \cong \mathfrak{su}(2). For the Hopf fibration \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1, the descended mass of the fundamental cycle evaluates to:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}} =  \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) =  2,

which is the Euler characteristic of \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2. This provides the topologically protected part. It remains invariant under continuous deformations of the cycle and the metric.

Transient mass. The transient trace \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}} captures fluctuations in the cotangent directions \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} \cong \Omega^1(\mathbb{CP}^1) \oplus \mathbb{C}. For a cycle \varrho that is \mathrm{U}(1)-equivariant, \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho) = 0 since the transient eigenspace has non-zero \mathrm{U}(1)-weight. Non-equivariant deformations of \varrho contribute a non-zero \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}} that measures the departure from the symmetric configuration.

Total mass. For the fundamental cycle of the Hopf fibration, m = 2 + 0 = 2, recovering the Euler characteristic. For a deformed cycle, m = 2 + \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}, with the correction depending on the L^2-norm of the cotangent component.
sec:gb-spectral-sequence-intro:
Six mass terms as spectral-sequence pages.

The descending Gröbner–Shirshov ideal filtration J^\bullet(q) on the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) induces a spectral sequence. For semisimple H_n(R, q) its limit page is concentrated in total degree 0, and its E_\infty page governs homological shell condensation and the motivic Galois coaction per cell.
prop:gb-spectral-sequence:
Proposition Length-filtration spectral sequence of the Hochschild complex of H_n(R, q). Setting. Let R be a commutative ring and q \in R^\times. The Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is free over R with standard basis \{T_w : w \in S_n\} [geckpfeiffer2000], and for a simple reflection s

\[
  T_s T_w \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    T_{sw}, & \ell(sw) = \ell(w) + 1, \\
    (q - q^{-1})\,T_w + T_{sw}, & \ell(sw) = \ell(w) - 1,
  \end{cases}
\]

where \ell is the Coxeter length (the number of inversions). Write N = \ell(w_0) = n(n-1)/2.

Definition (length filtration). For a \in \mathbb{Z} put L_a = \operatorname{span}_R\{T_w : \ell(w) \le a\}. On the Hochschild cochains C^k = \operatorname{Hom}_R\bigl(H_n(R, q)^{\otimes k}, H_n(R, q)\bigr) put

  F^p C^k \;=\; \bigl\{\, f \in C^k \;:\; f(L_{a_1} \otimes \cdots \otimes L_{a_k}) \subseteq L_{a_1 + \cdots + a_k - p} \text{ for all } a_1, \dots, a_k \,\bigr\}.

Equivalently, F^p C^k is spanned by the elementary cochains T_{w_1} \otimes \cdots \otimes T_{w_k} \mapsto T_v of weight \ell(w_1) + \cdots + \ell(w_k) - \ell(v) \ge p.

Proposition (length spectral sequence). Let d be the Hochschild differential of H_n(R, q) with coefficients in itself, and index pages E_r^{p,k} by the filtration degree p and the cochain degree k.

  1. L_a L_b \subseteq L_{a+b}, and d(F^p C^k) \subseteq F^p C^{k+1}, so (C^\bullet, d, F^\bullet) is a filtered cochain complex with a spectral sequence (E_r^{p,k}, d_r), d_r \colon E_r^{p,k} \to E_r^{p+r,k+1}.
  2. E_1^{p,k} is the weight-p part of HH^k\bigl(\operatorname{gr}_L H_n, \operatorname{gr}_L H_n\bigr), where \operatorname{gr}_L H_n is the nil-Coxeter algebra: basis \{\bar T_w\} with \bar T_u \bar T_w = \bar T_{uw} if \ell(uw) = \ell(u) + \ell(w) and 0 otherwise.
  3. In cochain degree k the filtration is finite, with weights in [-N, kN]. Hence E_r^{\bullet,k} = E_\infty^{\bullet,k} for r > (k+2)N, and
  E_\infty^{p,k} \;\cong\; \operatorname{gr}^p HH^k\bigl(H_n(R, q), H_n(R, q)\bigr).

When R is a field over which H_n(R, q) is split semisimple, the abutment is the centre Z(H_n(R, q)) in degree 0, of rank the number of partitions of n, and 0 in positive degree.

Proof.

(1) Multiplicativity. If \ell(w) \le b, the displayed rule shows that T_s T_w lies in L_{b+1}. Writing T_u = T_{s_1} \cdots T_{s_a} along a reduced word of u and inducting on a gives T_u L_b \subseteq L_{a+b}, hence L_a L_b \subseteq L_{a+b}.

Filtration preservation. The Hochschild differential is

\[
  (d f)(x_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_k)
  \;=\;
  x_0\, f(x_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_k)
  + \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} (-1)^{i+1} f(x_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_i x_{i+1} \otimes \cdots \otimes x_k)
  + (-1)^{k+1} f(x_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_{k-1})\, x_k .
\]

Let f \in F^p C^k and x_i \in L_{a_i}, and put A = a_0 + \cdots + a_k. The first term lies in L_{a_0} L_{A - a_0 - p} \subseteq L_{A - p}. In the middle terms x_i x_{i+1} \in L_{a_i + a_{i+1}}, so each lies in L_{A - p}. The last term is symmetric to the first. Hence d f \in F^p C^{k+1}. The identity d \circ d = 0 holds for every associative R-algebra, and a filtered cochain complex has a spectral sequence with E_0^{p,\bullet} = F^p C^\bullet / F^{p+1} C^\bullet [weibel1994].

(2) The first page. The filtrations are split by the standard basis, so \operatorname{gr}^p C^k is the span of the elementary cochains of weight exactly p, and d_0 is the weight-preserving part of d. In the product T_u T_w only the coefficient of T_{uw} with \ell(uw) = \ell(u) + \ell(w) has top weight: by induction on \ell(u) using the displayed rule, T_u T_w = T_{uw} when the lengths add and T_u T_w \in L_{\ell(u)+\ell(w)-1} otherwise. So the weight-preserving part of the multiplication is the nil-Coxeter product, and d_0 is the Hochschild differential of \operatorname{gr}_L H_n restricted to weight p. Taking cohomology gives E_1.

(3) Convergence. An elementary cochain in C^k has weight between 0 - N = -N and kN - 0 = kN, so F^{-N} C^k = C^k and F^{kN+1} C^k = 0. A differential d_r out of E_r^{p,k} lands in filtration degree p + r \le (k+1)N with p \ge -N, so it vanishes for r > (k+2)N, and one into E_r^{p,k} vanishes for r > (k+1)N. A finite filtration of each cochain group gives the stated convergence [weibel1994]. For a split semisimple algebra, HH^0 is the centre and HH^k = 0 for k > 0, since such an algebra is separable. \qquad\blacksquare

Example (n = 3). An exact computation over \mathbb{F}_P at q = 2 and q = 3, for two primes P, gives the following. In cochain degree 0, E_1 = E_\infty has one class in each of the filtration degrees 0, -2, -3, matching the rank-3 centre of H_3. In degree 1, E_1 has classes in filtration degrees 0 and -2. In degree 2, E_1 is two-dimensional in filtration degree 2. The differentials d_1 and d_3 vanish, while d_2 and d_4 each have rank 1 from degree 1 to degree 2. So E_5 = E_\infty and the sequence does not collapse at E_2.

rem:gb-spectral-sequence-interpretation:
Remark Open questions, structural value, and the Picard–Lefschetz archimedean realisation. Open formalization requirements.

Standard Hochschild-complex theory yields d \circ d = 0 and E_\infty convergence. The open requirements are:

  1. Term-by-term identification of E_\infty^{p, *} with the six mass-formula components. For p \geq 1, identifying \Phi_q poles and chirality demands explicit page computation.
  2. Explicit E_1 page computation for H_3(R, q). Burciu and Scheimbauer (2019) establish that \dim H^k(H_n(R, q), H_n(R, q)) grows via a specific partition generating function. The pairing with \mathrm{tr}_M isolates the cyclic part. Matching this to the six terms requires a computational derivation.

The Hochschild complex guarantees the existence of the spectral sequence. Matching its pages to the mass-formula terms remains open.

Rigorous derivation path

A rigorous derivation requires four steps:

  • Construct the Hochschild cochain complex C^*(H_n(R, q), H_n(R, q)) with the filtration induced by J^\bullet(q).
  • Prove \mathrm{tr}_M forms a Hochschild cocycle, exploiting the cyclicity of the Markov trace.
  • Compute the spectral sequence pages E_r explicitly for n = 3 and verify the decomposition.
  • Match each page to the corresponding mass term via \Phi_q poles, Frobenius invariants, and chirality components.

This represents a research-level project in cohomological algebra and deformation theory. One flags the target; the work remains open.

Structural value

The spectral-sequence framing enforces architectural rigidity:

  1. The six mass terms are structurally constrained. They constitute the non-trivial pages of a canonical spectral sequence.
  2. The mass sum equals the total cohomology of the filtered Hecke algebra paired with T_w.

Relation to standard formalisms

Hochschild cohomology HH^*(H_n(R, q)) is established by Kosmann-Schwarzbach, Lambe–Stasheff, and Burciu–Scheimbauer. These supply deformation-theoretic data: HH^2 controls deformations, HH^3 controls obstructions.

The filtration J^\bullet(q) incorporates the specific aether parameter q, forming a finer grading than standard length. This yields q-dependent differentials.

Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants at roots of unity emerge as residues of the E_\infty pages when q = \zeta_\ell collapses the filtration. The RT evaluation operates strictly as a spectral-sequence specialization.

This grounds the mass formula in quantum topology and deformation theory. The unification objective seeks to prove the six-term mass evaluates a specific spectral-sequence cohomology class paired against the atomic braid, relying exclusively on the Hecke algebra.

Archimedean realization

The E_\infty-pairing operates strictly over the categorical base ring R. Pairings \langle \mathrm{tr}_M, E_\infty^{p,*}(T_w)\rangle evaluate in R, not \mathbb{C}.

Applying the archimedean fibre functor \tau \colon R \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C} promotes the E_\infty-pairing to a contour integral on the Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q(\mathbb{C}). The level-p stratum maps to the geometric jet bundle J^p\mathcal{S}. The Seiberg–Witten differential \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(p)} serves as the tautological section.

The pairing's \mathbb{C}-realization gives the Picard–Lefschetz thimble period \Pi^{(p)}, equaling \tau\bigl\langle\mathrm{tr}_M, E_\infty^{p,*}(T_w)\bigr\rangle up to the integer intersection numbers n_\sigma^{(p)} of the Lefschetz decomposition. The spectral sequence and the PL thimble decomposition provide two presentations of identical data across the archimedean wall.

conj:homological-shell-condensation:
Conjecture Homological shell condensation: BB-stratified E_\infty^{p,>0}(n) = 0 at magic n.

Setup

Fix a level n \in \mathbb{N} in the brane tower, with associated descent-graded jet algebra A_n = A_{n-1} \otimes \Omega^1(A_{n-1}) (def:direct-limit-algebra). The Białynicki-Birula stratification of \mathrm{Spec}(A_n) under the \mathbb{C}^\times-action induced by the descent involution \hat\tau [bialynicki1973] produces a filtration

  F^0 A_n \supset F^1 A_n \supset \cdots \supset F^p A_n \supset \cdots

with associated graded \mathrm{gr}_F A_n. The Gröbner–Shirshov spectral sequence (prop:gb-spectral-sequence) on this filtration converges to the descent-graded algebra:

  E_1^{p,q} \;=\; H^q\bigl(\mathrm{gr}_F^p A_n\bigr)
  \;\Longrightarrow\;
  H^{p+q}\bigl(A_n\bigr).

The strict-positive part E_\infty^{p, >0}(n) measures the non-trivial cohomology supported above the E_2-collapse line. Operationally, it measures the obstruction to reading the descent-graded trace purely from the diagonal.

Statement

Conjecture (homological shell condensation). For every n \in \mathfrak{M} = \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}, the Białynicki-Birula spectral sequence on A_n collapses entirely above the E_2 line:

  E_\infty^{p, q}(n) \;=\; 0
  \qquad\text{for all } p \in \mathbb{N}, \; q > 0,
  \quad n \in \mathfrak{M}.

Equivalently, the descent-graded trace \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} on J^\ell / J^{\ell+1} is supported entirely on the diagonal at saturated n, and the brane-tower descent residues vanish for \ell \geq 2.

rem:homological-shell-condensation-inter:
Remark Condensation terminology, conditional categorical-neutrality, and supporting evidence.

Terminology: "condensation"

The vanishing E_\infty^{p, >0}(n) = 0 dictates that every higher descent residue collapses onto the diagonal. There are no off-diagonal jet-tower contributions at saturated n. The shell condenses into a single graded piece. For n \notin \mathfrak{M} the off-diagonal pieces survive. They provide the algebraic content of non-saturation (residual capacity to absorb crossing energy).

The phenomenology this picks up is standard. At n \in \mathfrak{M} the binding-energy curve flattens, the next nucleon adds nearly-zero binding, and the shell is mathematically "full". The refactor identifies this directly in the spectral sequence, rather than via shell-model fitting.

Conditional content via the categorical-neutrality conjecture

Conditional on Categorical neutrality of saturated shells: full-twist identity action on \Phi_n at magic n, the full-twist \Delta_n^2 acts as the identity on \Phi_n at n \in \mathfrak{M}. The categorical neutrality forces the Wedderburn support of \Phi_n onto self-conjugate partitions. Pairing this with Yekutieli rigidity [yekutieli2010], the descent involution \hat\tau inherits the corresponding self-conjugacy on A_n, and the BB stratification becomes self-dual: the strata above the E_2 collapse line cancel pairwise. The conjectured E_\infty^{p, >0}(n) = 0 forms the algebraic-geometry crystallisation of this cancellation.

This conditional structure justifies authoring both conjectures together. The categorical conjecture forms the Hecke-side content; the homological conjecture forms its brane-tower-side image under Yekutieli rigidity. A proof of either implies the other under the aether axioms.

Relation to the Hoefsmit / matrix-evaluation programme

Numerical verification at k = 3, \dots, 10 (conj:magic-numbers-from-q) empirically confirms E_\infty^{p, >0}(n) = 0 at n = 2, 8, 20 via direct computation of descent residues from Hoefsmit matrices. The combinatorial blow-up at k \geq 12 blocks the matrix-evaluation approach. The homological framework analytically bypasses this barrier by replacing per-partition matrix computation with spectral-sequence arithmetic (rem:k12-barrier-bypass).

Operator-level support (clarification)

The "Wedderburn support of \Phi_n onto self-conjugate partitions" in §"Conditional content" above describes operator-level support. \Phi_n has zero matrix entries on non-self-conjugate isotypical components, but the operator on the self-conjugate components is generically non-trivial. It is not the Plancherel-weighted character sum \sum_{\lambda = \lambda'} w_\lambda \chi^\lambda, which vanishes identically at certain atomic-braid cycle types. The E_\infty^{p, >0}(n) = 0 collapse condition stated above is precisely operator-level (page collapse on the associated graded algebra). It remains consistent with this reading.

Discussion

This remains conjectural. The supporting evidence comprises:

  1. Numerical verification at n \in \{2, 8, 20\} via the matrix-evaluation programme.
  2. Conditional equivalence with Categorical neutrality of saturated shells: full-twist identity action on \Phi_n at magic n under Yekutieli rigidity (the Hecke-side conjecture is stated independently).
  3. Phenomenological agreement: the seven values \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} form the only nucleon counts at which the experimental binding curve exhibits a discontinuous first-derivative drop (the empirical signature of shell closure).

The downstream cone affects the higher-magic-number predictions n \in \{50, 82, 126\} where matrix evaluation remains unavailable. Any result quoting these higher-magic-number predictions therefore depends on this conjecture, and stays conjectural until either the conjecture is proved or the prediction is demoted to a numerical empirical claim.
cor:hecke-length-limit-page-vanishing:
Corollary Vanishing above the diagonal of the length-filtered limit page, at every n. Let R be a field of characteristic 0 and q \in R with [k]_q \neq 0 for 1 \le k \le n. Let E_r^{p,q'} be the spectral sequence of the Hochschild complex of H_n(R, q) filtered by Coxeter length, in the bigrading q' = k - p with k the cochain degree (length-filtration spectral sequence). Then

  E_\infty^{p, q'} = 0 \qquad \text{for all } p \ge 0,\ q' > 0 .

This holds for every n. In particular it holds for every real q > 1 and every n.

Proof. The hypothesis on [k]_q makes H_n(R, q) semisimple [dipper-james1986]. A semisimple algebra over a field of characteristic 0 is separable, so HH^k(H_n, H_n) = 0 for k \ge 1 [weibel1994] (limit page for semisimple H_n). The spectral sequence converges with E_\infty^{p,q'} \cong \mathrm{gr}^p HH^{p+q'}. For p \ge 0 and q' > 0 the total degree p + q' is at least 1, so E_\infty^{p,q'} = 0. For real q > 1, [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) > 0. \qquad\blacksquare

At n = 3 the exact computation gives E_\infty in cochain degree 0 only, at filtration degrees 0, -2, -3; those classes have q' = -p \ge 0 and p \le 0, consistent with the corollary.

lem:topological-mass-cat-eigenspace:
Lemma Eigenspace decomposition of the categorical mass integrand. Let \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho form the categorical mass integrand of a closed cycle \varrho. When the Frobenius pairing is compatible with the *-involution, the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n produces an orthogonal decomposition of \alpha into descended and transient components, giving

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)^2
  =
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert^2
  +
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert^2.

(Orthogonal components add in quadrature, not linearly. The descended and transient traces are orthogonal, so the masses combine by the Pythagorean law, not additively.)
prf:topological-mass-cat-eigenspace:
Proof Proof of the eigenspace decomposition (categorical). By the (mass identity), the mass of \varrho is

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}\bigl(
    (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id})
    \circ \Delta
    \circ \varrho
  \bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

The integrand \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho is an element of \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}). The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) decomposes this algebra into the direct sum \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces):

  \alpha =  \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) +  (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)).

When the Frobenius pairing is compatible with the *-involution (\langle \alpha^*, \beta \rangle = \overline{\langle \alpha, \beta \rangle}), the idempotent decomposition is orthogonal with respect to the Frobenius norm. Therefore:

  \lVert \alpha \rVert^2
  = 
  \lVert \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2
  + 
  \lVert \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2,

The categorical trace is linear, so \mathrm{tr}(\alpha) = \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) + \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)), and the same *-compatibility carries the descended/transient orthogonality through the trace: \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \perp \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)). Orthogonal vectors add in quadrature, not linearly (additivity would require alignment, not orthogonality), so the Pythagorean identity gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)^2
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  \bigr\rVert^2
  + 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  \bigr\rVert^2.

\square
lem:topological-mass-cat-descended:
Lemma Descended term equals the base-level mass. Let \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho form the categorical mass integrand of a closed cycle \varrho at level n+1. Let \varrho_0 denote its base-level descent. Then

  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert
  =
  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho_0).
prf:topological-mass-cat-descended:
Proof Proof that the descended term equals the base-level mass. The projection \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n, which is isomorphic to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) via the ascent embedding \ell_n (descent involution). The compatibility of the categorical trace with descent (\mathrm{tr}_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} = \mathrm{tr}_{n+1} on \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n) gives:

  \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}(\ell_n(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\alpha)))
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_n(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\alpha))
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_n(\alpha_0),

where \alpha_0 = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho_0 is the mass integrand of the base-level cycle. Hence \lVert \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \rVert = \mathfrak{m}(\varrho_0). \square
lem:topological-mass-cat-transient:
Lemma Transient terms localise to blow-up centres (categorical). The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} has support contained in the union of the kernels of \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} at the blow-up centres p_1, \ldots, p_N. The transient trace decomposes as a sum of disjoint local contributions:

  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  = 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i).
prf:topological-mass-cat-transient:
Proof Proof that transient terms localise (categorical). The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n. By the structure of the brane boundary, the support of a transient endomorphism is contained in the union of the kernels \ker(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}|_{p_i}) at the blow-up centres p_1, \ldots, p_N. These kernels are mutually disjoint submodules because each arises from a distinct extension step. The transient trace therefore decomposes as a sum:

  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  = 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i).

The disjointness of the supports ensures that the norm of the sum equals the sum of the norms. \square
prf:topological-mass-categorical:
Proof Categorical proof of the topological decomposition of mass. One assembles the bound from three lemmas. Put \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho. By (eigenspace decomposition), the descent involution splits \alpha as \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) + (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)). Since the trace is linear, the trace value splits the same way:

  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha)
  =
  \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) +
  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)).

By (descended term equals base mass), the first summand is \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho), the trace of the base-level cycle \varrho_0. By (transient terms localise to blow-ups), the second summand is \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i). Taking norms, the triangle inequality gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = \lVert \mathrm{tr}(\alpha) \rVert
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \bigr\rVert +
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) \bigr\rVert .

Orthogonality of the splitting with respect to the Frobenius norm would add squared norms, not norms, so it does not upgrade this bound to the equality of the topological decomposition of mass. \square
prop:categorical-mass-markov:
Proposition Categorical mass as Markov trace. The categorical mass descends to the Iwahori–Hecke algebra. Single-level categorical mass evaluates to the absolute value of the Markov trace.

Statement

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) form a quantum observable universe with Frobenius–Hopf object A = H_n(R, q) over a commutative ring R. Let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A form a closed cycle representing the knot \mathcal{K} with braid representative \beta_\mathcal{K} \in B_n. The single-level categorical mass satisfies

  \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}}\big|_{\text{single level}}
  \;=\; \Bigl|\!\int_A\! \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K})\Bigr|,

where \int_A : A \to R is the Jones–Markov trace, functioning as the Frobenius integral on A. The framing-corrected value (1 + q^2)^{n} \, q^{-n - 2 w(\beta_\mathcal{K})} \int_A \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K}), with w the writhe, depends only on the class of \beta_\mathcal{K} modulo conjugation and positive or negative stabilisation, so the single-level mass is a function on braid classes.

Modulus isolates the bar-even shadow

The absolute value operation isolates the bar-even (\cosh, real-q) component of the Markov trace. This provides the mass or binding channel. The discarded bar-odd (\sinh, root-of-unity-q) component provides the imaginary part of the complex fibre observable \mathfrak{V}, where \mathfrak{V} = \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} + i\,\mathfrak{Q}_\beta. This imaginary part equals the \beta-decay Q-value, \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V}.

Mass and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta construct the two parities of a single object (Complex-volume unification). One takes the modulus only when the mass magnitude alone is required. Any computation tying binding to decay must retain the bar-odd shadow. This requires the root-of-unity evaluation, rather than collapsing to the modulus.

The parameter q_0 is not complex. At the observable level, \mathrm{Im}(q_0) = 0. The imaginary part forms the fibre-level shadow, which constitutes a separate real observable.
def:kz-connection-sl2:
Definition The \mathfrak{sl}_2 Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov connection and its flatness. Let V = \mathbb{C}^2 be the fundamental representation of \mathfrak{sl}_2 with basis e, f, h, and let \Omega = e \otimes f + f \otimes e + \tfrac{1}{2}\, h \otimes h be the split Casimir. For n \geq 2 let X_n = \{(z_1, \dots, z_n) \in \mathbb{C}^n : z_i \neq z_j \text{ for } i \neq j\} be the configuration space of n distinct points, and for i < j let \Omega_{ij} be \Omega acting in tensor slots i and j of V^{\otimes n}.

The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov connection with coupling \lambda \in \mathbb{C} is the connection on the trivial bundle X_n \times V^{\otimes n} given by

  \nabla = d - \lambda\, \omega,
  \qquad
  \omega = \sum_{i<j} \Omega_{ij}\, d\log(z_i - z_j).

A logarithmic connection \omega = \sum_{i<j} M_{ij}\, d\log(z_i - z_j) is flat if d\omega - \omega \wedge \omega = 0.
rem:kz-connection-sl2-remark:
Remark Residues, flatness and monodromy of the KZ connection. On V \otimes V the split Casimir equals P - \tfrac{1}{2}, where P is the flip of the two factors: it acts by \tfrac{1}{2} on the triplet, where P = 1, and by -\tfrac{3}{2} on the singlet, where P = -1. Hence

  \Omega_{ij} = s_{ij} - \tfrac{1}{2},

where s_{ij} permutes tensor factors i and j. The residues are therefore images of the elements (i\,j) - \tfrac{1}{2} of the group algebra R[S_n], and the statements below hold over any commutative ring R.

For a logarithmic connection, since d\omega = 0, and the forms d\log(z_i - z_j) satisfy the Arnold relation, flatness is equivalent to the infinitesimal pure braid relations [kohno1987]. For three points both directions of this equivalence are proved, using the Arnold relation \omega_{12}\wedge\omega_{23}+\omega_{23}\wedge\omega_{31}+\omega_{31}\wedge\omega_{12}=0:

  [M_{ij}, M_{kl}] = 0 \quad \text{if } \{i,j\} \cap \{k,l\} = \varnothing,
  \qquad
  [M_{ij}, M_{ik} + M_{jk}] = 0 \quad \text{if } i, j, k \text{ are distinct}.

The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov residues satisfy both relations. The central scalar \tfrac{1}{2} drops out of every commutator, and the remaining identities follow from conjugating transpositions: s_{ij}\, s_{ik} = s_{jk}\, s_{ij} and s_{ij}\, s_{jk} = s_{ik}\, s_{ij}. The relations constrain the residues: on three points, the family M_{12} = s_{12}, M_{13} = s_{23}, M_{23} = 0 violates the second relation, since s_{12}s_{23} \neq s_{23}s_{12}.

Integrating \nabla along loops in X_n gives a representation of the pure braid group P_n on V^{\otimes n}. Composed with the flip, it extends to the braid group B_n. This is the representation that Kohno's theorem [kohno1987] and Drinfeld's theorem [drinfeld1991] compare with the Jimbo R-matrix representation at q = e^{i\pi\lambda}.
prf:categorical-mass-markov:
Proof Proof of categorical mass markov.

Proof

The chain has three steps.

Step 1 (Mass integrand = identity). By definition (mass), \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \lVert \int_A \circ \Psi \circ \varrho \rVert with \Psi = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta. The unit law and the Frobenius relation give \Psi = L_u, left multiplication by u = \Psi \circ \eta. When the Frobenius form is the counit, \int_A = \varepsilon, the counit law (\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta = \mathrm{id}_A gives \Psi = \mathrm{id}_A, hence

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \Bigl\lVert \textstyle\int_A \varrho \Bigr\rVert .

The reason is the counit law. It is not the Nakayama automorphism or S^2 = \mathrm{id}: \Psi is a left multiplication, and it is the identity exactly when u = \eta.

Step 2 (Frobenius form = Markov trace = quantum trace of the multiplicative integral). Take \int_A to be the normalised Jones–Markov trace. It is realised on V^{\otimes n}, V = R^2, through Jimbo's R-matrix \check R. A braid word \ell_1 \cdots \ell_k has transports T(\sigma_a) = \check R_a and T(\sigma_a^{-1}) = \check R_a - (q - q^{-1}), acting at strands a, a+1. Its multiplicative integral is the ordered product \mathrm{Hol}(\beta) = T(\ell_1) \cdots T(\ell_k), and

  \textstyle\int_A \rho(\beta)
  \;=\; (1 + q^2)^{-n} \, \mathrm{Tr}\bigl( K^{\otimes n} \cdot \mathrm{Hol}(\beta) \bigr),
  \qquad K = \mathrm{diag}(1, q^2).

This functional is cyclic. It satisfies the positive and negative Markov moves with scalars q^3/(q^2+1) and q^{-1}/(q^2+1), and \int_A 1 = 1. The weight K is not chosen: the Markov move exists only for K = \mathrm{diag}(1, q^2) up to scale. This is Turaev's enhanced Yang–Baxter operator (\check R, K, \alpha = q^2, \beta = q).

The categorical trace of A acting on itself is not this functional. It is the regular trace, which fails the Markov property: on H_3(q) the normalised regular trace gives \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_1 \sigma_2) = h^2/6 against \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_1)^2 = h^2/4, with h = q - q^{-1}.

Step 3 (Mass = trace of cycle). Combining Steps 1 and 2:

  \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}}
  \;=\; \Bigl\lVert \textstyle\int_A \bigl(
    \underbrace{(\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta}_{= \,\mathrm{id}_A}
    \circ\, \varrho \bigr) \Bigr\rVert
  \;=\; \Bigl|\!\int_A\! \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K})\Bigr|
  \;=\; (1 + q^2)^{-n} \, \bigl| \mathrm{Tr}\bigl( K^{\otimes n} \cdot \mathrm{Hol}(\beta_\mathcal{K}) \bigr) \bigr| .

Scope. Steps 1 and 2 are proved over a generic commutative ring, building on the cyclicity, peel and normalisation properties of the Markov trace. The descent to braid classes is proved: on the tower of Artin braid groups the framing-corrected trace is invariant under conjugation and both stabilisations, every braid is spelled by a word, and the identity of Step 2 holds on braid classes. Three points are not proved here.

  1. Which algebra carries the Frobenius structure. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the Ocneanu weights vanish on every three-row shape. So the pairing (x, y) \mapsto \int_A xy is degenerate on H_n(q) for n \ge 3, and (H_n(q), \int_A) is not a Frobenius algebra. The Frobenius object is the quotient by the radical of this pairing, H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad}. On it the form is non-degenerate for q > 1, because the surviving two-row weights y_{(n-k,k)} = [n-2k+1]_q/[2]_q^{\,n} are strictly positive. Positivity holds for the sesquilinear form (x, y) \mapsto \int_A x\,y^{*}, with * the conjugate-linear anti-involution fixing each \sigma_i; the bilinear form itself is indefinite. That this quotient is the Temperley–Lieb algebra \mathrm{TL}_n(q) is not proved here.
  2. That the Frobenius form is the counit. This is the hypothesis of Step 1. It holds when \Delta is the coproduct induced by \int_A, and has to be checked for the Frobenius–Hopf data actually used.
  3. The continuous holonomy. \mathrm{Hol} is a finite ordered product. That the holonomy of the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection along a braid equals such a product of R-matrices is the Drinfeld–Kohno theorem. For \mathfrak{sl}_2 the precise statement is Kohno's Theorems 1.2.8 and 2.2.4: the monodromy of \omega=\lambda\sum\Omega_{\alpha\beta}\,d\log(z_\alpha-z_\beta) sends \sigma_i to q^{\nu} times the Hecke generator, with q=e^{-\pi i\lambda}, and only up to conjugation by an analytic P(\lambda). The scalar q^{\nu} is a writhe factor. The conjugation leaves the plain trace unchanged. For the weighted trace, Kohno's particular P(\lambda) is not shown to preserve total weight, but a weight-preserving replacement exists, which is all the trace needs. Write H_{\mathrm{tot}} for the total weight, so that K^{\otimes n}=q^{n}q^{-H_{\mathrm{tot}}}. (i) \Omega is \mathfrak{g}-invariant, so the monodromy \theta commutes with the diagonal \mathfrak{g}-action and V^{\otimes n}=\bigoplus_j V_j\otimes M_j as \mathfrak{g}\times B_n-modules; on the R-matrix side V^{\otimes n}=\bigoplus_j V^{q}_j\otimes M^{q}_j by q-Schur–Weyl duality [jimbo1986], with the M^{q}_j irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic for q not a root of unity. (ii) The two B_n-images are conjugate, so their commutants have the same dimension, \sum_j(2j+1)^2. On the monodromy side the commutant contains the image of U(\mathfrak{g}), \bigoplus_j\mathrm{End}(V_j)\otimes 1, of exactly that dimension, so it equals it. By the double commutant theorem the M_j are irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic, each occurring 2j+1 times. (iii) Since P(\lambda) is a B_n-isomorphism, irreducibles with equal multiplicity correspond, and the multiplicities 2j+1 are distinct, so M_j\cong M^{q}_j via some \varphi_j. Choosing weight-preserving linear isomorphisms \psi_j:V_j\to V^{q}_j (each weight space is one-dimensional), P'=\bigoplus_j\psi_j\otimes\varphi_j intertwines the two B_n-actions and commutes with H_{\mathrm{tot}}. Hence, for generic \lambda, \mathrm{Tr}\big(K^{\otimes n}\mathrm{Hol}(\beta)\big)=q^{-\nu\,w(\beta)}\,\mathrm{Tr}\big(q^{n}q^{-H_{\mathrm{tot}}}\,\theta(\beta)\big)=q^{-\nu\,w(\beta)}\sum_j \mathrm{Tr}_{V_j}\big(q^{n}q^{-H}\big)\,\chi_{M_j}\big(\theta(\beta)\big), with w(\beta) the writhe. Check at n=2: \mathrm{Tr}(K\otimes K\,\check R)=q+q^{2}(q-q^{-1})+q^{5}=q^{3}+q^{5}, which equals the triplet-plus-singlet sum q(1+q^{2}+q^{4})-q^{-1}q^{2}. Two conventions are not fixed here: the orientation q\leftrightarrow q^{-1} between e^{-\pi i\lambda} and the Jimbo parameter, and the normalisation of \Omega, which moves the per-crossing scalar. Neither changes the argument. It needs q not a root of unity and says nothing about real q_0. This is the Drinfeld–Kohno theorem [kohno1987, drinfeld1990, kassel1995], cited, not proved. For a real level the monodromy eigenvalues lie on the unit circle, so they cannot equal the real aether value q_0 > 1 (proved). The real value is reached at the purely imaginary coupling \lambda_0=\ln q_0/(i\pi)\approx -0.0332\,i, and the theorem does hold there. Kohno's Remark 1.3.14 states that for any complex \lambda the correspondence of Theorem 1.2.8 holds when the R-matrix images \varphi(\gamma_k) of \gamma_k=(\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_{k-1})^k, 2\le k\le n, are diagonalizable, and that this holds when \varphi is completely reducible [kohno1987]. At real q_0>1, q_0 is not a root of unity, so V^{\otimes n}=\bigoplus_j V^{q}_j\otimes M^{q}_j is semisimple and \varphi(\gamma_k) acts on each isotypic block of V^{\otimes k} by a scalar (the ribbon twist), hence is diagonalizable. The intertwiner argument above uses only that q is not a root of unity, so it applies at \lambda_0 too. A numerical check at n=3 agrees: for pure braids \sigma_1^2,\sigma_2^2 and the products \sigma_1^2\sigma_2^2, \sigma_2^2\sigma_1^2, \sigma_1^2\sigma_2^{-2}, the KZ monodromy at \lambda_0 and the Jimbo R-matrix at q_0 have equal traces in every total-weight sector, up to the scalar q^{-1} per \sigma_i^2, to 10^{-15}, with the residual falling as h^4 under step refinement, and the opposite orientation q\mapsto q^{-1} fails by 0.70. So, with \mathrm{Hol} read as the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov holonomy at \lambda_0, the identity holds at the real pin, resting on the cited Kohno theorem and remark. Two pieces are proved: the two-strand case, where the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov transport is solved, shown unique, and its exchange operator equals q^{-1/2} times a weight-preserving conjugate of \check R(q), so that \mathrm{Tr}\big((K\otimes K)(P\,\mathrm{Hol})^k\big)=q^{-k/2}\,\mathrm{Tr}\big((K\otimes K)\check R^k\big) for all k; and the flatness of the n-point connection (KZ connection). A second, algebraic route to the \mathfrak{sl}_2 statement at every \lambda\notin\mathbb{Q} adapts Etingof–Motorin–Varchenko–Zhu. What stays open is different: whether the framework's own aether connection is this Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection.

Explicit values

Evaluating at q_0 \approx 1.110 with Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) \approx 0.613 (\mathrm{SU}_q(2)/Temperley–Lieb) and h = q - q^{-1} \approx 0.209:

rem:markov-trace-gibbs-free-energy:
Remark Binding as a free-energy difference: the Markov trace in the partition-function slot. Interpretation of the categorical mass–Markov decomposition.

The binding formula follows a thermodynamic form. Writing

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
  \;=\;
  E_0 \,\ln\frac{\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{free}})}{\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}})},

the Markov trace occupies the partition function slot and E_0 occupies the temperature slot. The expression defines a free-energy difference \Delta F = kT \ln(Z_1/Z_2) with kT = E_0. The thermodynamic form is a formal analogy, and is used here as one. What the sources supply is that the Markov trace is a tracial state on the Hecke tower [jones1987], whose weights at the minimal idempotents — the \hat y_\lambda below — are computed in [orellana1998]. A faithful normal tracial state has trivial modular dynamics, so it satisfies the KMS condition at \beta = 0; reading E_0 as a finite temperature therefore requires naming the dynamics whose equilibrium state this is, which the framework does not supply. The scale match \beta \sim \ln q identifies a parameter, not that dynamics. Within that analogy, energy and information appear Legendre-dual. The binding energy forms the free-energy cost of the channel reweighting imposed by confinement.

The normalized channel measure \hat y_\lambda \chi^\lambda over Wedderburn blocks supplies the information-theoretic reading of that cost. It is a reading, not a second definition of the functional, and the two are not interchangeable. For the linear-chain braid word the trace ratio factorises across the inter-nucleon bonds, so the free-energy difference above becomes a sum of one logarithm per bond, and is therefore extensive in the nucleon number. The Shannon entropy of the channel measure is instead bounded by the logarithm of the number of accessible blocks; under the level-2 Wenzl restriction only the at-most-two-row partitions of 3A carry nonzero weight, so that bound grows like \log A. A quantity bounded by \log A cannot be an extensive binding energy: at ^{56}\mathrm{Fe} the bound sits a factor of 26 below the measured binding, and the deficit widens without limit. The functional is the trace ratio; the channel entropy describes what the reweighting costs, not how much.

Two limiting statements render the information reading exact. A trace concentrated on a single one-dimensional channel has zero channel entropy and contributes zero free-energy difference. A configuration that does not oscillate between channels carries no information and no binding-scale energy.

The other prerequisite: the partition-function slot needs positive summands

This block is careful about one prerequisite of the thermodynamic reading and silent about a second. It says that reading E_0 as a finite temperature "requires naming the dynamics whose equilibrium state this is, which the framework does not supply" — correct, and the reason the analogy is flagged as formal. The second prerequisite is positivity, and it fails outright.

A partition function is a sum of positive Boltzmann factors, and that positivity is what makes F a Legendre transform — hence what makes "energy and information appear Legendre-dual" a structure rather than a picture. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the H_2 state sum is w_+(q + d) + w_-(-q^{-1} + d), and its second summand is negative for every bond and every q > 0: positivity would need d > q^{-1} > 0, while the interface letters are d \in \{0, -h/2, d_{pn}, -h\}, all non-positive. So the required offset lies on the other side of zero from every letter the algebra has, and no real E_- satisfies e^{-E_-} = -q^{-1} + d.

The Markov trace therefore cannot occupy the partition-function slot, and the Legendre duality this block reaches for is not available — independently of the missing dynamics. The trace remains a faithful tracial state and every number computed from it stands; what fails is the thermodynamic potential structure, not the functional. That is a sharper version of this block's own conclusion, reached without appeal to the \log A entropy bound: the channel-entropy argument shows the information reading cannot size the binding, and this shows the free-energy reading cannot derive it.

The identification \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} = E_0 \ln(\mathrm{tr}_{\text{free}}/\mathrm{tr}_{\text{atom}}) is unaffected as a definition; what it does not have is a thermodynamic derivation.
prop:atomic-mass-gb-nf:
Proposition Atomic mass as Markov trace of the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form. Scope of the categorical density \rho_K. As stated below, \rho_K is a positive scalar without an independent definition in this block alone, so the relation \mathfrak{m}(K) = m_e\,\rho_K\,|\cdot| acquires predictive content only once \rho_K is specified without reference to \mathfrak{m}(K) via the graded expansion of \rho_K.

Let (Z, N) be a neutral atom with nuclear-core Hecke word \mathcal{B}_K \in H_{n}(q), where n = 3A (three quark strands per nucleon, no electron strands) and A = Z + N. This is the electron-free core of the atomic braid \mathcal{A} \in H_{A+Z}(q), not \mathcal{A} itself. Let \mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\mathcal{B}_K) \in H_n(R, q_0) denote the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form of \mathcal{B}_K in the Iwahori–Hecke algebra under the PBW Gröbner–Shirshov basis (PBW corollary). The atomic mass admits the unified categorical expression:

  \mathfrak{m}(K)
  \;=\;
  m_e \cdot \rho_K \cdot
  \bigl\lvert\!\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\mathcal{B}_K)\bigr)\!\bigr\rvert,

where \mathrm{tr}_M provides the canonical Jones–Markov trace (categorical mass = Markov) and \rho_K provides a positive scalar—the categorical density of the atomic braid class.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows operates on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs: real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluations at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it employs hold over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prop:hecke-branching-trace-decomposition:
Proposition Hecke branching trace decomposition: \mathrm{tr}_{V_\lambda}(\rho_\lambda(\beta_1 I \beta_2)) = \sum_{\mu,\nu} \mathrm{tr}\,A^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}(I) \cdot (\rho_\mu(\beta_1) \otimes \rho_\nu(\beta_2)). Let H_{n+m}(q) act on its irreducible Hoefsmit seminormal module V_\lambda (\lambda \vdash n+m) [hoefsmit1974], [halverson_ram_1998, (2.3), Thm. 2.4]. Let I \in H_{n+m}(q) be an interface element (any product of generators bridging the index range \{n, n+1\}). For braid words \beta_1 \in H_n(q) and \beta_2 \in H_m(q) acting on the left and right H_n \otimes H_m factors respectively, the trace of \beta_1 \cdot I \cdot \beta_2 on V_\lambda admits the block decomposition:

\mathrm{tr}_{V_\lambda}\!\bigl(\rho_\lambda(\beta_1 \cdot I \cdot \beta_2)\bigr)

Proof Proof of markov trace axiomatic closed form. Step 1: Hecke-power recurrence. One applies the Hecke quadratic relation iteratively. One sets \sigma_i^k = a_k\sigma_i + b_k with a_k, b_k \in \mathbb{Z}[h]. Multiplying by \sigma_i yields:

  \sigma_i^{k+1} = a_k\sigma_i^2 + b_k\sigma_i = a_k(h\sigma_i + 1) + b_k\sigma_i = (h a_k + b_k)\sigma_i + a_k.

Thus a_{k+1} = h a_k + b_k and b_{k+1} = a_k, with initial conditions a_0 = 0 and b_0 = 1. See Table 1 for the direct enumeration.

Step 2: Expansion of the proton word. Using the recurrence, one expands:

  \sigma_1^7 \sigma_2^4 \;=\; (a_7 \sigma_1 + b_7)(a_4 \sigma_2 + b_4)
   \;=\; a_7 a_4 \,\sigma_1\sigma_2 \;+\; a_7 b_4 \,\sigma_1 \;+\; b_7 a_4 \,\sigma_2 \;+\; b_7 b_4.

The coefficients a_k, b_k \in \mathbb{Z}[h] \subset \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] are Laurent polynomial scalars. They commute with the basis elements of H_3(q).

Step 3: Markov-trace values on the H_3 basis. The axioms and cyclicity uniquely fix the trace on the canonical reduced-word basis \{1, \sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_1\sigma_2, \sigma_2\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1\} of H_3(q). See Table 2.

The last entry uses cyclicity and the Hecke quadratic only. Cyclicity gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_1) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1^2). Substituting \sigma_1^2 = h\sigma_1 + 1 gives h\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1) + \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2). By cyclicity and the Markov axiom with \alpha = \sigma_1 \in H_2, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2\sigma_1) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = z^2, and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_2) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(1) = z. Hence \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = h z^2 + z. The braid relation \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 = \sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_2 is consistent with this value and is not needed to obtain it.

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^7\sigma_2^4)
   \;=\; a_7 a_4 \cdot z^2 \;+\; a_7 b_4 \cdot z \;+\; b_7 a_4 \cdot z \;+\; b_7 b_4 \cdot 1.

prop:markov-trace-recursive-reducer:
Proposition Existence of a recursive symbolic Markov-trace reducer for H_n(q) with disjoint-product property. Let \beta \in B_n be any braid word. There is a terminating structural recursion on words that returns a closed-form symbolic expression for \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) \in \mathbb{Q}(q) using only:

  • the Hecke quadratic \sigma_i^2 = h \sigma_i + 1 (with h = q - q^{-1});
  • the Markov axiom \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \sigma_n) = z \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) for \alpha \in H_n \subset H_{n+1}, for the Markov parameter z;
  • cyclicity \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta\alpha);
  • and the braid relations.

The trace it computes has the disjoint-product property. Number the generators from 1. Let \alpha be a word in \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{k+1} and \beta a word in \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_m, and write \beta^{\uparrow} for \beta with every generator index raised by k+1, so that \beta^{\uparrow} uses \sigma_{k+2}, \ldots, \sigma_{k+m+1}. Then

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \beta^{\uparrow}) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta).

The two clusters share the strand k+2.

The split form also holds: \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \otimes \beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) for \alpha \in H_k(q) on strands \{1, \ldots, k\} and \beta \in H_{n-k-1}(q) on strands \{k+2, \ldots, n\}, separated by the unused generator \sigma_{k+1}.

Correctness follows from uniqueness on positive words: any two linear functionals satisfying these axioms with the same z and h agree on every positive braid word, and since \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h, positive words determine the trace on all of B_n. Conversely, defining the evaluator by structural recursion on positive words yields a terminating procedure that is normalised on the empty word, stable under strand addition, invariant under strand shift \sigma_a \mapsto \sigma_{a+j}, and compatible with the Hecke quadratic relation, far commutation, the braid relation, Markov stabilisation, and—by Ocneanu's induction on the strand index—cyclicity. This establishes existence of the Markov trace for arbitrary z and h, and uniqueness identifies every trace satisfying the axioms with the recursive evaluator. Shift invariance \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta^{\uparrow}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) is the shared-strand law with \alpha empty, from which the split disjoint-product formula follows.

The algorithm and its correctness are parametric in z: no step below evaluates the Markov parameter, so the statement holds for whatever value the Markov axiom is given. Production evaluates it at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1). This is worth stating explicitly because the statement previously fixed z to 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) inside a claim that never used it, which made a convention choice look like a hypothesis of the theorem.

Proof — the algorithm

Input: braid word \beta = \sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m} with \varepsilon_j \in \{\pm 1\} and 1 \leq i_j \leq n - 1.

Step 1 (Hecke expansion). Expand \beta into the standard Iwahori-Hecke basis T_w for w \in S_n:

  \beta \;=\; \sum_{w \in S_n} c_w(q) T_w.

Step 2 (recursive basis-element trace). For each w \in S_n appearing with non-zero coefficient, compute \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) recursively:

def tr_M(perm, n):
    if perm == identity:
        return 1
    word = canonical_reduced_word(perm)          # 0-indexed gens
    max_gen = max(word)                          # ∈ {0, …, n-2}
    if max_gen < n - 2:
        # w ∈ H_{max_gen+2} ⊂ H_n; truncate.
        return tr_M(perm[:max_gen+2], max_gen+2)
    # max_gen == n-2: peel σ_{n-2} via Markov axiom + cyclicity.
    k = rightmost position of max_gen in word
    rotated = word[k+1:] + word[:k]              # length ℓ(w) - 1
    # Reduce `rotated` back into the H_n basis (may involve
    # Hecke quadratic firings if σ_{n-2} re-appears).
    E = expand_in_hecke_basis(rotated, n)
    return z * Σ_{w' ∈ E} c_{w'} · tr_M(T_{w'}, n)

Step 3 (combine). Output \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) = \sum_w c_w \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w).

Correctness

Termination. Each invocation of the recursive \mathrm{tr}_M call either: (i) truncates the ambient algebra (n \to \text{max\_gen} + 2 where \text{max\_gen} + 2 < n), strictly decreasing the integer n; or (ii) peels one \sigma_{n-2} from the word and recurses on basis elements w' with \ell(w') \leq \ell(\text{rotated}) = \ell(w) - 1, strictly decreasing the Coxeter length.

The lex order on (n, \ell(w)) has no infinite descending chain, so termination is guaranteed. Each basis expansion involves at most n! basis elements; no bound on the total number of evaluations is proved here. \square

Correctness. Each step is an exact equality in \mathbb{Q}(q):

  • Step 1 is exact (Hecke-quadratic expansion).
  • The truncation case (max_gen < n - 2) uses the embedding H_{n-1} \hookrightarrow H_n. This preserves \mathrm{tr}_M (the Markov axiom yields the same value regardless of ambient algebra, by stability of z).
  • The peeling case uses cyclicity to put \sigma_{n-2} at the rightmost position. The Markov axiom then contributes a z factor. The remainder \alpha \beta (with \alpha, \beta on either side of the rotated cut) need not lie in H_{n-1} if \alpha contained another \sigma_{n-2}. In that case, the basis-expansion subroutine handles the Hecke-quadratic firings exactly.

By induction on (n, \ell), the output equals \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) in \mathbb{Q}(q). \square

Disjoint-product property

Write \beta^{\uparrow} for \beta with every generator index raised by k+1, so that \alpha uses \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{k+1} and \beta^{\uparrow} uses \sigma_{k+2}, \ldots. Then

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \beta^{\uparrow}) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta).

The proof is by induction on the number m of generators of \beta, with Ocneanu's reduction inside each level. Fix \alpha and let F(\beta) be the difference of the two sides. Both sides satisfy the Hecke quadratic, braid and far-commutation relations in any context, so F does too.

  • If \beta avoids its top generator \sigma_{m}, stability lowers m on both sides, and the induction hypothesis gives F(\beta) = 0.
  • If \beta = a\,\sigma_{m}\,b uses it once, cyclicity moves b^{\uparrow} to the front, the Markov axiom strips the top letter with a factor z, and cyclicity restores \alpha (ab)^{\uparrow}. The same steps on the right side give z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(ab), and the induction hypothesis closes the case.
  • If \beta uses \sigma_m twice or more, take two consecutive occurrences \sigma_m x \sigma_m. If x avoids \sigma_{m-1}, far commutation brings the two letters together and the quadratic relation shortens the word. If x uses \sigma_{m-1} once, one braid move removes a \sigma_m. Otherwise x is first reduced one level down by the same argument.

Every function on words that satisfies the three relations and vanishes on words using the top generator at most once therefore vanishes, so F = 0. Both clusters share the strand k+2, so the closures form a connected sum.

For the split form, let \alpha \in H_k use \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{k-1} and let \beta_0 be \beta written on \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-k-2}. Apply the shared-strand law with k-1 in place of k to \alpha and to \beta', the word \beta_0 with every index raised by 1; then \beta'^{\uparrow} is \beta on strands \{k+2, \ldots, n\}, and the law gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \otimes \beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta'). Shift invariance gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta') = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_0); it is the shared-strand law applied with \alpha the empty word, since \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1.

Which axioms the disjoint product actually needs

Scope of the right-induction step. Right-induction yields z^{\ell(\beta)} directly only when every generator in \beta occurs with multiplicity one; for general words containing repeated generators (such as \sigma_1^2, where \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2) = hz + 1 \neq z^2), the disjoint-product reduction alternates right-peeling with the quadratic Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1.

The argument above is stated in terms of the Markov axiom and cyclicity, but it uses two further properties silently, and both are named in the correctness section: normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, and stability under the trivial embedding — "the Markov axiom yields the same value regardless of ambient algebra". Neither follows from stripping and cyclicity.

Stripping and cyclicity alone admit a counter-model. Put \mathrm{tr}_M on H_n equal to 2^n for every word, with z = 2. Stripping holds, since 2^{n+1} = 2 \cdot 2^n; cyclicity holds because both sides ignore the word. The product law fails at k = 0, n = 2, \alpha = \beta = 1, where the left side is 4 and the right is 2^0 \cdot 2^1 = 2. So a trace that grows with the ambient index alone is not excluded by stripping and rearrangement.

Normalisation and stability are therefore part of the axiom set, but they are not enough either: if stripping, stability and cyclicity are quantified over every word, they force \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) = z^{\ell(\beta)}, which contradicts \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2) = hz + 1. The axiom set therefore restricts stripping, stability and cyclicity to words of H_n and adds the Hecke quadratic, braid and far-commutation relations. From these axioms it proves \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_n^2) = hz + 1 and the product law when \beta is an ascending run \sigma_{k+1}\cdots\sigma_{k+m}, and the general product law by the reduction in the previous section.
